question: At fixed chemical transition rates and local reservoir parameters, how does selectively changing the permitted hopping frequency of each material conformation affect late spatial lengths, region count, and realized chemistry?
preregistration: Frozen before mobility histories or any new length measurements. Reuse the N48/T3000 uniform_minus reference through T1800. Retain all histories. Same initial state by case at each seed and physical settings at t=0.
results: In each seed, report paired changes in spectral length, half-correlation, resolved count at both thresholds, width-4 variance, B fraction, work rate, and gross and signed reaction rates. The intervention only rescales existing detailed-balance-compatible hops in one conformation. If abs(delta B) exceeds 0.02 label the contrast as combined transport/composition. With a smaller difference detailed composition and reaction kinetics can still vary; do not treat comparisons as proof of independent slopes or a microscopic mechanism.
bounds: Diffusion of the solvent-proxy fuel and waste and both chemical pathways keep their original parameters. Vary the rate of forward and reverse hops together; no orientation, region label, or configured boundary is used.
